name: cc-enforcer
description: Rules your coding agent physically cannot ignore. A Claude Code plugin (and LLM-agnostic rule pack) that stops reactive patching, guessed citations, surface-level fixes and premature "done" claims by intercepting the agent's own tool calls — PreToolUse denies the edit before it lands, and a nine-layer Stop gate refuses to let a completion claim end the turn without evidence, a convergence self-quiz, a fidelity check against the original request, and a one-line TL;DR. Twelve rules, eight of them backed by a hook; per-project "Imperial Edict" regexes you define yourself; a repo-wide sync gate; CI drift gates that derive every documented number from the code so the docs cannot rot. Zero dependencies, stdlib only, and every guard fails OPEN — a bug in the discipline can never brick your agent. v0.35.2 registers a fourth co-update group in this repo's own sync gate — `hooks/scripts/*_guard.py` now requires a README sweep, asserted by the user rather than guessed by the scanner, because a guard's user-visible behaviour is enumerated in both READMEs and v0.35.1 is the release that found out what happens when it is not. Writing that gate also produced its own instance of the class it closes: the new checks made three behavioural claim classes derivable, while the gate's own design notes still declared prose behaviour and citation accuracy uncoverable wholesale — so `test_doc_sync`'s docstring, `tests/README.md` and `docs/README.md` were swept together, and the note now separates the derivable sub-classes from the judgement prose that genuinely is not checkable. 682 tests, unchanged. Prior — v0.35.1 is a documentation-truth release: the active half of rule 12 (the repo-refresh full-repo scan) was run for the first time since v0.32.2, and it found that both READMEs advertised a detector that does not exist. The layer-(b) row named "should be fine" and "应该" as hedges, the before/after demo was built on "Should be stable now", and the sample output claimed `Hedge matched: 'Should be'` — but bare `should` is deliberately excluded from the hedge set, as stop_guard's own comment says, so the demo's OUTPUT could not have been produced by its own INPUT. v0.34.1 had aligned the injected PROMPTS down to the implementation and scoped that sweep to prompts/; the READMEs describe the same detector and were never in it. Two more of the same class: the rolling-patch sample printed a per-file coverage bar of "1104 of 3672 chars" where the code computes 1102, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's decision table cited four block-reason constants deleted in v0.12.0 and cited for the twenty-three releases since. Correcting the words would decay again, so each class got a gate instead: hedge trigger examples are now derived from stop_guard._HEDGE_INNER, sample coverage bars from lib/editscale.coverage_bar, and every backticked UPPER_SNAKE identifier in a non-CHANGELOG doc must exist in the repo's Python or be registered as a doc-only exception with a reason. All three were verified RED against the pre-fix tree — a gate that only passes on fixed content cannot tell a working check from a deleted one. This description was also trimmed: it had accumulated nine stacked release narratives duplicating CHANGELOG.md, the same second-source defect CLAUDE.md §6.1 fixed for itself in v0.30. 676 -> 682 tests. Full release history: CHANGELOG.md.
